report_name: Advisory Warns of Prolific SafePay Ransomware Targeting Critical Infrastructure

threat_actors.name: SafePay ransomware group
threat_actors.description: A highly active ransomware group operational since at least August 2024, responsible for compromising approximately 600 organizations globally, including critical infrastructure sectors. The group uses common intrusion methods like credential theft, exploiting known vulnerabilities, and phishing.
threat_actors.goals: Financial extortion through ransomware deployment and data encryption.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: Targeting unpatched vulnerabilities in internet-facing systems like VPNs for initial access.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: Using stolen or guessed credentials to log into legitimate services like Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP).

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: Using phishing campaigns designed to steal user credentials for initial access.

attack_patterns.name: Windows Command Shell
attack_patterns.description: Using cmd.exe for executing commands and scripts on victim systems.

attack_patterns.name: Disable or Modify Tools
attack_patterns.description: Attempting to disable or uninstall security software such as antivirus and EDR on endpoints to avoid detection before deploying ransomware.

attack_patterns.name: Remote Desktop Protocol
attack_patterns.description: Using RDP to move laterally between systems on the victim network.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: Encrypting files across the network to disrupt business operations and demand a ransom.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: The ransomware actors delete volume shadow copies using tools like vssadmin.exe and wmic.exe to prevent system recovery from backups.

attack_patterns.name: Brute Force
attack_patterns.description: The group uses password guessing and credential stuffing against exposed services to gain initial access.

attack_patterns.name: Create Account
attack_patterns.description: The actors create new user accounts to maintain persistence within the victim network.

malware.name: SafePay ransomware
malware.description: The ransomware payload deployed by the SafePay group to encrypt files on victim networks and demand payment for a decryptor.

tools.name: vssadmin.exe
tools.description: Used to delete volume shadow copies to prevent system recovery.

tools.name: wmic.exe
tools.description: Used as an alternative command to delete volume shadow copies.

tools.name: bcdedit.exe
tools.description: Used to modify boot configuration data to inhibit system recovery by ignoring all boot failures.

identities.name: critical infrastructure sectors
identities.description: A primary target category for the SafePay ransomware group, spanning multiple sectors globally across the Americas, Europe, and Australia.

indicators.name: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
indicators.pattern:
title: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
id: 2b9a1b3c-8d4e-4f6a-9b1c-5d6e7f8a9b0c
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common precursor to ransomware deployment as used by SafePay ransomware.
references:
  - https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa26-293a
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-21
tags:
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.impact
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'delete'
      - 'shadows'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a technique used by SafePay ransomware to inhibit system recovery.

indicators.name: BCDEdit Recovery Disablement
indicators.pattern:
title: BCDEdit Recovery Disablement
id: 1a2b3c4d-5e6f-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of bcdedit.exe to ignore boot failures, a technique used by ransomware to inhibit system recovery.
references:
  - https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa26-293a
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-21
tags:
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.impact
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\bcdedit.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/set'
      - 'bootstatuspolicy'
      - 'ignoreallfailures'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of bcdedit.exe to set the boot status policy to ignore all failures, a technique used to inhibit system recovery.

indicators.name: Windows Failed Logon Attempt
indicators.pattern:
title: Windows Failed Logon Attempt
id: f0e9d8c7-b6a5-4b3c-8d2e-1f0a9b8c7d6e
status: experimental
description: Detects a failed logon attempt (Event ID 4625). High volumes of this event can indicate password guessing or spraying attacks as seen with SafePay ransomware.
references:
  - https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa26-293a
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-21
tags:
  - attack.t1110
  - attack.credential_access
level: low
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 4625
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects Windows Event ID 4625, which indicates a failed logon attempt. High volumes of this event can be a sign of brute force attacks.
